subject: springboot
question: In an executable Spring Boot jar, what does the manifest's Main-Class point to?
options: Your @SpringBootApplication class directly
org.apache.catalina.startup.Bootstrap
Spring Boot's JarLauncher, with Start-Class naming your application class
java.lang.ClassLoader
explanation: The launcher sets up a class loader for the nested jars and then invokes Start-Class.

subject: springboot
question: Why does @WebMvcTest(UserController.class) fail with NoSuchBeanDefinitionException for UserService?
options: UserService must be annotated with @RestController
The slice does not load @Service beans, so the dependency must be mocked
MockMvc requires services to be static
@WebMvcTest forbids constructor injection
explanation: Provide UserService with @MockitoBean (or @MockBean in older versions) so the controller can be created.

subject: springboot
question: What does spring.profiles.group.prod=proddb,prodmq do?
options: It creates a prod profile only when proddb and prodmq are both active
It merges the three profiles' files into one file at build time
It disables proddb and prodmq when prod is active
Activating prod also activates proddb and prodmq
explanation: Profile groups let one logical profile expand into several more specific profiles.

subject: springboot
question: With spring-boot-starter-parent, how do you usually override the managed version of Jackson?
options: Edit the starter jar's MANIFEST.MF
Set the jackson-bom.version property in the pom
Add @JacksonVersion to the main class
Delete the dependencyManagement section
explanation: The parent manages versions through properties, so redefining one changes the version used.

subject: springboot
question: What is the default phase of a @TransactionalEventListener?
options: BEFORE_COMMIT
AFTER_COMMIT
AFTER_ROLLBACK
AFTER_COMPLETION
explanation: The listener runs only after the publishing transaction commits successfully, unless another phase is set.

subject: springboot
question: What effect does setting management.server.port=9091 have?
options: All endpoints are disabled except health
The app moves to port 9091 and actuator stays on 8080
Actuator endpoints are served on a separate port from the application
Metrics are pushed to a server on port 9091
explanation: A separate management port lets you keep operational endpoints off the public network.

subject: springboot
question: Why can adding different @MockitoBean declarations across test classes slow a test suite?
options: Mockito must recompile classes for each mock
Mocks disable parallel test execution
Mocks force a full Maven rebuild
Each unique mock set changes the context cache key, forcing new contexts
explanation: Spring's test context cache reuses a context only when configuration, including bean overrides, is identical.

subject: springboot
question: A public method in OrderService calls this.placeOrder(), which is @Transactional. No transaction is active beforehand. What happens?
options: A new transaction starts as normal
placeOrder runs without a transaction because the call bypasses the proxy
Startup fails because of self-invocation
Spring starts a nested transaction
explanation: Self-invocation goes straight to the target object; use a separate bean, self-injection or AspectJ mode.

subject: springboot
question: How do you make @DataJpaTest use the real database configured in your properties instead of an embedded one?
options: Use @SpringBootTest alongside it
Add @Transactional(propagation = NEVER)
Set spring.jpa.show-sql=true
Add @AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = Replace.NONE)
explanation: By default @DataJpaTest replaces any DataSource with an embedded one; Replace.NONE keeps yours.

subject: springboot
question: An app defines two SecurityFilterChain beans. How does Spring Security pick which one handles a request?
options: Both chains run in sequence for every request
The chain declared last in the class always wins
The first chain, by @Order, whose securityMatcher matches the request
It merges the chains into one
explanation: FilterChainProxy uses the first matching chain, so specific matchers need higher precedence than catch-all chains.
